output.subject: We've received your message about access at our Depot Square branch
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for taking the time to write to us. We have received your complaint, and we want you to know that it has been read carefully.

You told us that you use a wheelchair and that the accessible entrance at our Depot Square branch has been blocked by a large planter for months. You mentioned that on September 23 you knocked on the window and asked staff for help getting in, and that the manager told you to "come back with someone who can help you." You said you ended up doing your banking on your phone in the parking lot, and that you shouldn't need a chaperone to get into your own bank.

We're sorry for the frustration and distress this experience has caused you. A specialist team is now reviewing your complaint, and we will respond to you within 10 business days.

Thank you again for bringing this to our attention.

Kind regards,
Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Draft is acknowledgment only; it takes no position on what happened on September 23 or on the entrance.
Decide whether the branch should be contacted now to check and clear the accessible entrance, separately from the formal response.
Confirm whether the customer needs any interim alternative way to access in-branch services before the full response.
Check whether the customer needs correspondence in an accessible format.
The manager is referred to by role only; their name was withheld in the complaint and is not included in the reply.
Customer raised disability access; consider whether legal or accessibility specialists should review before the substantive reply.
